answer: Hypothesis (final answer): In all three wealth measurement years — 1985, 1990, and 1996 — individuals with a criminal record, proxied by ever_jailed = 1 (jailed at least once between 1985 and 1994), had significantly lower composite wealth than individuals without such a record (ever_jailed = 0). Mann–Whitney U (two-sided) on the full sample of 12,013 NLSY79 respondents gave p = 1.6e-10 (1985), 7.8e-35 (1990), and 9.3e-26 (1996); all three remain significant after Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction at q = 0.05 (adjusted p ≤ 4.8e-10) and under Bonferroni. The jailed group's median wealth was lower in every year (e.g., $0 vs $10,500 in 1990; $0 vs $8,500 in 1996; $720 vs $3,600 in 1985), with rank-biserial effect sizes of 0.22–0.42. This is an observational association: the 1985 wealth measurement is contemporaneous with the start of the jailing window (1985–1994) and thus largely pre-treatment, so the 1985 gap reflects pre-existing socioeconomic differences (selection into incarceration) rather than a causal effect of jailing; ever_jailed is a narrower proxy than a full criminal record (it excludes non-custodial records).

payload.workflow: 1) Inspected data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv: 12,013 rows, 6 columns, zero missing; ever_jailed 289 (1) vs 11,724 (0); race white/black/hispanic (7099/3013/1901, 'hipanic' treated as hispanic); sex 6164/5849. Wealth composites (sums of five NLS components) are extremely right-skewed (skew 6.5-16.8), with 25-38% exact zeros and negative values (debt), ruling out log-transforms and motivating rank-based inference. 2) Primary analysis per year: Mann-Whitney U two-sided comparing composite wealth of ever_jailed=1 vs 0 on the full sample; effect sizes: difference in medians and rank-biserial correlation, with means reported secondarily. 3) Multiple-testing: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR at q=0.05 across the three years as decision rule, with Bonferroni reported for reference. 4) Sensitivity: Welch t-test per year; stratified MWU by race (3 strata) and by sex (2 strata), reported only as robustness checks. 5) Result: all three years (1985, 1990, 1996) show significantly lower wealth for the jailed group under both corrections; stratified checks confirm robustness in 11 of 12 strata (not significant in black 1985 at raw alpha, though the jailed median is still lower). Executed script: analysis/main_analysis.py; results table: analysis/results_primary.csv.
